name: Wi-Fi access points
label: Wi-Fi
notes: Wi-Fi access points (IEEE 802.11), decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. One job reads one 20 MHz channel: start it on a channel's centre with a band of 20 MHz (the handler takes 20 MHz of IQ, the receiver's minimum; the frequency picks the band). An event is a beacon, a probe response or a FILS discovery frame, the frames an access point is read from: `frame_type`, `bssid` (12 hex digits), `ssid` (null for a hidden network), `channel` (the beacon's own channel element, else the radiotap frequency's), `freq_hz`, `security` (OnAir's word: `Open`, `WEP`, `WPA`, `WPA2`, `WPA2/WPA3`, `WPA3`, `OWE (Enhanced Open)`, an enterprise one with `-Enterprise`; null on a FILS discovery frame, which has none) and `len`. There is no data rate: OnAir's radiotap header has none, so the rate a frame was received at is not known. Every frame whose FCS passed, data frames too, goes to a packet capture (a radiotap header and the 802.11 frame, link type 127); nothing is decrypted. Ranges and bands: the 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz bands (2400 to 2483.5, 5150 to 5895 and 5925 to 7125 MHz) are IEEE 802.11's, across regions, and a 20 MHz channel is the narrowest an 802.11 receiver reads; only the 2.4 GHz scene has a test signal, so the 5 and 6 GHz paths (OFDM, several channels in a wide input) are untested. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 0.46 of a core and the node 0.46 of a core (load average 3.8 to 4.7, with another build running).
